\## Mutation

\`#106 MATHEMATICAL\_INTRINSICS\`, stacked on #105.

## Implementation

- adds strict \`chronus.ir.v0.2\` intrinsic nodes for Fibonacci, Lucas, exact Binet, Zeckendorf encode/decode, Cassini verification, Pisot scheduling, and phi weighting
- preserves \`chronus.ir.v0.1\` unchanged
- canonicalizes the existing Aethel exact implementations rather than copying divergent algorithms
- keeps exact Binet distinct from approximate floating phi/psi paths
- validates u64 domains (\`Fibonacci/Binet 0..93\`, \`Lucas 0..92\`) before dispatch
- enforces canonical non-adjacent 93-bit Zeckendorf representations over full u64
- makes Cassini consume actual supplied witnesses and reject mutations
- keeps conventional planner candidates beside Lucas/Pisot proposals; measurement remains promotion authority
- adds dedicated OpenCL lowering sources and per-intrinsic capabilities; all physical states remain \`PHYSICAL\_EVIDENCE\_REQUIRED\`, while \`BINET\_EXACT\` is honestly unsupported there
- extends the same #104 case/corpus formats and content-addressed authority instead of creating a second test universe
- adds tests, machine-readable capabilities, semantic/truth-boundary documentation and \`python scripts/check\_chronus106.py\`

## ISA and encoding boundary

No Chronus-1 v1.1 opcode is added. Chronus-1 wide-integer lowering fails closed because the accepted ISA cannot yet express it safely. The compiler emits canonical plans, never machine words; any future Chronus-1 lowering must go through the accepted assembler.

## Truth boundary

New Python sources passed local syntax compilation. Repository tests and inherited gates remain \*\*NOT RUN\*\* because this agent environment cannot clone the repository or resolve github.com. Intel/OpenCL execution remains \`PHYSICAL\_EVIDENCE\_REQUIRED\`; f64 remains rejected by #104; \`cl\_khr\_fp64\` is not certification; \`FOLDED\_NATIVE\` remains OPEN. CI remains \`NOT\_REPORTED\` until GitHub reports it.

## Acceptance

\`\`\`bash
python scripts/check\_chronus106.py
\`\`\`
